lens: Salesforce Lightning-adjacent: CRM-native feel, record pages, works inside sales tools
name: Call Record Console
one_liner: Salesforce-style record pages for practice: every call is a live, coached record, every persona is a browsable CRM-like record, and the OpenAI models are named where they act.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed the Lightning lens: record-page structure (highlights header, Path stage bar, activity-timeline transcript, related lists with counts, docked utility panel, left icon rail, list views with filter chips) and CRM-native objects (Persona, Scenario, Call Record, Rubric, Member). Changed: a dark-first console instead of Lightning's white enterprise chrome, because live calls need low glare and the product should read as AI-native. No Salesforce logo or trade dress. Self-scores: A 8, B 8, C 7, D 6 (only if the coach channel is under about 2.5s), E 5.5 (only with 80+ seeded personas), F1 6, F2 7 (BPO and training-company demand is documented), F3 3.

design_language.typography: Geist Sans: 15px body at 1.5 line height; 28/34 headings at weight 600 with -0.02em tracking. Geist Mono 13px for timers, scores, timestamps and evidence line numbers.
design_language.shape_and_depth: 10px radius on controls, 14px on records and panels, 1px hairline borders, elevation from surface steps rather than shadows. Retire the blurred gradient orb; the live indicator becomes a real audio level meter.
design_language.motion: Cue cards slide in over 180ms ease-out from the right. Score ring and rubric bars tween over 300 to 600ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion, use opacity only. No looping decoration.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react at 1.75px stroke: 20px in controls, 16px in chips. A single amber spark glyph marks all coach output so reps learn the signal.
design_language.theme_modes: Dark is the default for live call, landing and records. Light is for debrief print and docs. Driven by data-theme on html, with a prefers-color-scheme fallback. Tokens defined on :root.

live_coaching_and_scoring: The persona voice stays persona-only. A separate coach channel reads each finished turn and returns structured JSON: a one-line cue, a next best question, an objection tag, and rubric deltas, each with the transcript line that justifies it. Coach mode is Silent, Whisper or Full, set pre-call and changeable mid-call. Cues that arrive after about 2.5 seconds are dropped, not shown late. Live rubric numbers carry a 'live estimate' label until the final grade replaces them. If the grader falls back to heuristics, the debrief shows an Estimate chip instead of a letter grade. The coach model is configurable, so any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works.
persona_library_and_wizard: Library: 120 personas across 24 sales jobs and 15 industries (SDR cold call, AE discovery, CSM renewal, collections, recruiting, medical devices, solar, insurance, mortgage, home services, B2B procurement, retail and more), shipped as one JSON file per persona so contributors add them by pull request. Facets: sales job, industry, difficulty, objection type, call type, source. Wizard: step 1 accepts a URL, job description, CRM export, ICP text or a pasted call. Steps 2 to 4 fill persona, scenario and rubric, with a source snippet on each field. Step 5 is a 60-second text dry run, then Save to my library or Export as a PR-ready file. Ship at least 80 seeded personas before any public launch claim.
signature_moments: A Path bar that fills as the rep hits talk-track stages, the same component before, during and after the call.
Every score and coach cue links to the exact transcript line it came from.
Models named on the record: a Coach chip on the live console and a Graded by footer on each debrief.
Wizard fields show the source snippet they came from, so a generated persona reads like a cited brief.
openai_fund_angle: Models are named where they act: a Coach chip on the live console, a Graded by footer on every record, and a per-session token and cost panel in Settings so reviewers can see real OpenAI usage. Add the OpenAI Realtime API as a voice engine beside ElevenLabs Agents, and do not claim it on the landing page until it ships. For contributors: a persona JSON schema with a CI validator, a Good first persona label, and a Codex CLI task that drafts and validates persona files. That covers the PR-review and maintainer-automation workflow the Codex for Open Source program is meant to support.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 1: CSS-variable tokens, Geist fonts, shadcn primitives and dark theme; retire the orb and the globals.css component classes. Phase 2: live console and debrief record page on the existing trainer API. Phase 3: persona JSON library with list views and record pages. Move user-created scenarios from localStorage to Prisma once signed in. Phase 4: wizard, progress and team views, and the mobile bottom sheet. Compare each phase against docs/redesign/current screenshots.

risks: Lightning-style density can drift into CRM clutter. Cap visible panels at three per screen and keep the dark console calm.
Coach latency decides criterion D. If the coach channel misses about 2.5 seconds, the cue must drop rather than arrive late.

Persona realism: Hyperbound claims 2M+ hours of real call data, and a Reddit user called its roleplay unrealistic for B2B (https://www.reddit.com/r/sales/comments/1hvqu38/ever_used_ai_roleplaying_tools_like_hyperbound_or/). Hand-written personas need the pasted-call wizard and temperament controls to feel real.

Competition: Second Nature, Hyperbound, Yoodli, Mindtickle and Zenarate all sell roleplay. The open-source core must win on transparency, self-hosting and the live coach. Second Nature says its scored feedback arrives within about 90 seconds after a session, a vendor claim to verify.
Persona content is a labor project: 120 personas and rubric templates. Ship 80 before any public launch claim.
Voice is ElevenLabs today. Do not claim OpenAI Realtime on the landing page until the adapter ships.
Tremor: a third-party blog says it is joining Vercel. Check license, maintenance and Tailwind 3 compatibility before adopting.
Trade dress: borrow Lightning's structure, not its logo, blue chrome or Salesforce naming.
The heuristic grader fallback currently produces a letter grade (F at 50%). The fix belongs in scoring logic as well as the debrief UI.
